model.label: Segmented system: tax-financed SIS, EsSalud social insurance, armed forces and police, and private insurers

overview.statement: Peru has four main subsystems for financing and providing care: the tax-financed public sector (SIS), the contributory social insurer EsSalud, a smaller subsystem for the armed forces and police, and the private sector; each covers a different part of the population, with its own benefit package and providers.

overview.statement: The Seguro Integral de Salud (SIS) mainly covers people with low incomes and is financed from general taxation; on 5 March 2020 it covered 53% of Peru's roughly 33 million people, and its members are treated without charge in publicly owned, tax-financed providers.

overview.statement: EsSalud, the second largest insurance subsystem, covered 30% of the population on 5 March 2020; it covers workers in formal employment and their legal dependants, is financed by compulsory contributions of 9% of salary, and provides care free at the point of use.
